nodes.name: Tverberg partition / $r$-divisible set
nodes.statement: A finite set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ has a Tverberg partition into $r$ parts $X_1,\ldots,X_r$ if $\bigcap_{p=1}^r \mathrm{conv}\,X_p \ne \emptyset$; in this case $X$ is called $r$-divisible.
nodes.statement_clean: A set is r-divisible if it can be split into r parts whose convex hulls share a common point.

nodes.name: a-general position
nodes.statement: $X = \{a_1,\ldots,a_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is in a-general position if the $dn$ coordinates of the $a_i$ are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A point set is in a-general position when all its coordinates are algebraically independent.

nodes.name: Proper partition
nodes.statement: A partition $\mathcal{P} = \{X_1,\ldots,X_r\}$ of $X$ is proper if $1 \le |X_p| \le d+1$ for every $p \in [r]$.

nodes.name: Regular value $t_0$
nodes.statement: A value $t_0 \in [0,1)$ is regular if $X(t)$ is $r$-divisible for all $t \in [0,t_0]$ and the solution to $M(\mathcal{P}(t_0),t_0)(\alpha,z)=c$ satisfies $\alpha_i(t_0) > 0$ for all $i$.

nodes.name: Singular value $t_1$
nodes.statement: $t_1 > t_0$ is singular if it is the smallest $t > t_0$ at which either $\alpha_h(t_1)=0$ for some $h \in [n]$ or $\det M(t_1)=0$.

nodes.name: Block matrix $M(\mathcal{P})$
nodes.statement: $M(\mathcal{P})$ is the $(n+d)\times(n+d)$ block matrix whose $p$-th block $B_p$ has columns $(a_i,1)$ for $i \in J_p$, with $r$ further $-I_d$ blocks in the last $d$ columns; rows of all-ones separate blocks.

nodes.name: Tverberg's theorem
nodes.statement_latex: If $n=(r-1)(d+1)+1$ and $r\ge 2,\, d\ge 1$ are integers, then any $X = \{a_1,\ldots,a_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is $r$-divisible.
conclusions: $X$ is $r$-divisible: there is a partition $X_1,\ldots,X_r$ of $X$ with $\bigcap_{p=1}^r \mathrm{conv}\,X_p \ne \emptyset$

nodes.name: Tverberg in a-general position
nodes.statement_latex: If $X \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $|X|=n$ is in a-general position and $n=(r-1)(d+1)+1$, then $X$ is $r$-divisible.

nodes.name: Inductive moving step
nodes.statement_latex: If $\{b_1,a_1,\ldots,a_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is in a-general position and $\{a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n\}$ is $r$-divisible, then so is $\{b_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n\}$.

nodes.name: Radon's theorem
nodes.statement_latex: Any set of $d+2$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admits a partition into two sets whose convex hulls intersect (the case $r=2$ of Tverberg's theorem).
conclusions: $X$ admits a partition $X = X_1 \sqcup X_2$ with $\mathrm{conv}\,X_1 \cap \mathrm{conv}\,X_2 \ne \emptyset$

nodes.name: Affine intersection lemma
nodes.statement_latex: If $X \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $|X|=n$ is in a-general position and $\mathcal{P} = \{X_1,\ldots,X_r\}$ is a proper partition of $X$, then $\bigcap_{p=1}^r \mathrm{aff}\,X_p$ is a single point $z$. If $|X| < n$ under the same conditions, $\bigcap_{p=1}^r \mathrm{aff}\,X_p = \emptyset$.
conclusions: If $|X| = n$: $\bigcap_{p=1}^r \mathrm{aff}\,X_p$ is a single point

nodes.name: Nonsingularity of $M$ and $M_i$
nodes.statement_latex: If the partition of $X$ is proper, then $\det M \ne 0$ and $\det M_i \ne 0$ for all $i \in [n]$.

nodes.name: Sign of $\det M(t_0)$
nodes.statement_latex: For a regular value $t_0$ (after a fixed sign convention), $\det M(t_0) > 0$.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of vanishing index $h$
nodes.statement_latex: At a singular value $t_1 < 1$, $\alpha_h(t_1) = 0$ holds for a unique $h \in [n]$.

nodes.name: Matrix form $M(\alpha,z)=c$
nodes.statement_latex: $M(\alpha,z) = c$, where $M$ is the $(n+d)\times(n+d)$ block matrix and $c \in \mathbb{R}^{n+d}$ has $1$s in positions $d+1,2(d+1),\ldots,r(d+1)$ and $0$s elsewhere.

nodes.name: Cramer linearity in $t$
nodes.statement_latex: $\det M_i(t) = (1-t)\det M_i(0) + t\det M_i(1)$, a linear function of $t$.

nodes.name: Initial set construction (rotated regular simplices)
nodes.statement: Construct a $r$-divisible initial set $V^* \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ in a-general position by perturbing the union of $r-1$ randomly rotated regular simplices and the origin.
input: Optional given set $B$ in a-general position
output: Set $V^* \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of size $n=(r-1)(d+1)+1$ in a-general position with $v_n^* \in \bigcap_{p=1}^{r-1} \mathrm{conv}\,V_p^*$
$B \cup V^*$ in a-general position when $B$ is given

nodes.name: Moving-the-points algorithm
nodes.statement: Continuously move $a_1$ to $b_1$ along $a_1(t) = (1-t)a_1 + t b_1$, maintaining a Tverberg partition by swapping at each singular value, finishing with a partition for $X(1)$.
input: Target point $b_1$ with $\{b_1,a_1,\ldots,a_n\}$ in a-general position

nodes.name: Compatibility of initial set with given $B$
nodes.statement: If $B = \{b_1,\ldots,b_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is given in a-general position, the initial set $V^*$ can be chosen so that $B \cup V^*$ is in a-general position.

nodes.name: Finiteness of singular values
nodes.statement: The number of singular values is finite, since each is determined by a (proper) partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $X(t^*)$ and an index $h$ with $\alpha_h(t^*)=0$, and there are finitely many such pairs.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (nonsingularity of $M$, $M_i$)
nodes.statement: By Lemma~LP433.1 unique solution forces $\det M\ne 0$; if $\det M_i=0$ then by Cramer $\alpha_i=0$, contradicting the second part of LP433.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim $\det M(t_0) > 0$
nodes.statement: Show $M_1(t)$ is constant in $t$ and nonzero by algebraic independence; deduce $\det M(t_0)\ne 0$ from a rank argument, then use Cramer to fix the sign.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim (uniqueness of $h$)
nodes.statement: If two indices $h\ne i$ both have $\det M_h(t_1)=\det M_i(t_1)=0$, the linearity of $\det M_i(t)$ in $t$ forces a polynomial relation among coordinates, contradicting algebraic independence.

nodes.name: Proof of inductive moving step (TP433.3)
nodes.statement: Move $a_1$ along $a_1(t)=(1-t)a_1+tb_1$, track the Tverberg partition through the finite singular values; at each singular value swap one point between blocks to obtain a new regular value, eventually reaching $t=1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Tverberg in a-general position (TP433.2)
nodes.statement: Combine the initial-set construction (AP433.1) with the inductive moving step (TP433.3): repeatedly replace one $a_i$ by a target point, keeping a-general position and $r$-divisibility.

nodes.name: Proof of Tverberg's theorem (TP433.1) via limit
nodes.statement: A standard limiting argument (Tverberg's original) deduces the general statement TP433.1 from the a-general-position version TP433.2.

nodes.name: Set up homotopy and matrix $M(t)$
nodes.statement: Write $a_1(t)=(1-t)a_1+tb_1$, $X(t)=\{a_1(t),a_2,\ldots,a_n\}$, and let $M(t)=M(\mathcal{P},t)$ be the block matrix from EP433.2 for the current partition $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: Define regular values; $t_0=0$ is regular
nodes.statement: By Proposition PrP433.1 and a-general position, $t_0=0$ is a regular value: $\alpha_i(0)>0$ for all $i$, $\det M(0)\ne 0$.

nodes.name: Sign control: $\det M(t_0)>0$
nodes.statement: Apply Claim ClP433.1 (proved via PP433.2) to fix $\det M(t_0)>0$ after a column swap normalising $\gamma=\det M_1>0$.

nodes.name: Define and locate the next singular value $t_1$
nodes.statement: Let $t_1>t_0$ be the smallest $t$ where $\alpha_h(t_1)=0$ for some $h$ or $\det M(t_1)=0$. If $t_1\ge 1$ we are done; otherwise $t_1<1$.

nodes.name: Rule out $\det M(t_1)=0$
nodes.statement: If $\det M(t_1)=0$, then $\alpha_1(t)=\gamma/\det M(t)>1$ for $t<t_1$ near $t_1$ (since $\sum_i \alpha_i$-type bounds force it), contradicting feasibility.

nodes.name: Unique vanishing index $h$
nodes.statement: By Claim ClP433.2 (proved via PP433.3), there is a unique $h\in[n]$ with $\alpha_h(t_1)=0$.

nodes.name: Build $\overline{M}(t_1)$ and expand by column $h$
nodes.statement: Replace column $h$ of $M(t_1)$ by $(a_h,1,a_h,1,\ldots,a_h,1)$ (repeated $r$ times) to get $\overline{M}(t_1)$ with $\det \overline{M}(t_1)=0$, then expand: $0 = \det M(t_1)+\sum_{p\in J}\det\overline{M^p}(t_1)$.

nodes.name: Pick $j \in J$ with $\det\overline{M^j}(t)<0$ on $L(t_1,\eps_2)$
nodes.statement: Since $\det M(t_1)>0$, some $j\in J=\{p\ne q : |X_p|\le d\}$ has $\det \overline{M^j}(t)<0$ on a small interval to the right of $t_1$; set $M^*(t)=\overline{M^j}(t)$ and $\mathcal{P}^*=\mathcal{P}_j$.

nodes.name: All $\beta_i(t)>0$ on $L(t_1,\eps_3)$, so new regular value $t_2$
nodes.statement: On $L(t_1,\eps_2)$, $\det M^*(t)<0$, $\beta_h(t)>0$, and $\beta_i(t_1)=\alpha_i(t_1)>0$ for $i\ne h$; by continuity $\beta_i(t)>0$ for $t\in L(t_1,\eps_3)$, giving a new regular value $t_2 = t_1+\eps_3$.

nodes.name: Iterate to $t=1$ via finitely many singular values
nodes.statement: Iterate the singular-value swap; by Remark RP433.2 the number of singular values is finite, so $X(t)$ remains $r$-divisible for every $t\in[0,1]$, and in particular for $t=1$ giving $\{b_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n\}$ $r$-divisible.

nodes.name: Use linearity of $\det M_i(t)$
nodes.statement: Since $\det M_i(t)=(1-t)\det M_i(0)+t\det M_i(1)$ is linear in $t$, the singular value formula EP433.4 gives $t_1$ in terms of $\det M_i(0)$, $\det M_i(1)$.

nodes.name: Two indices give algebraic relation
nodes.statement: If both $h$ and $i$ vanish at $t_1$, equating the two formulas gives $\det M_i(0)\det M_h(1) = \det M_h(0)\det M_i(1)$, a non-trivial polynomial relation in the coordinates.

nodes.name: Contradict algebraic independence
nodes.statement: This polynomial identity contradicts the algebraic independence of the coordinates, so $h$ is unique.

nodes.name: Show $M_1(t)$ is constant and nonzero
nodes.statement: Replacing column 1 of $M(t)$ by $c$ removes the only $t$-dependent column, so $M_1(t)=\gamma$ is constant; algebraic independence gives $\gamma\ne 0$, and a column swap normalises $\gamma>0$.

nodes.name: Rank argument forces $\det M(t_0)\ne 0$
nodes.statement: Since the system $M(t_0)(\alpha,z)=c$ is consistent, $\mathrm{rank}\,M(t_0)=\mathrm{rank}\,[M(t_0),c]$; the latter contains $M_1(t_0)$ of full rank $n+d$, so $\det M(t_0)\ne 0$.

nodes.name: Cramer fixes sign of $\det M(t_0)$
nodes.statement: $\alpha_1(t_0)=\gamma/\det M(t_0) > 0$ (regularity) with $\gamma>0$ forces $\det M(t_0)>0$.

nodes.name: Unique solution iff $\det M\ne 0$
nodes.statement: By LP433.1, the affine intersection is a single point; equivalently the linear system EP433.2 has a unique solution, so $\det M\ne 0$.

nodes.name: Contradict via Cramer if $\det M_i=0$
nodes.statement: If $\det M_i=0$, then $\alpha_i=\det M_i/\det M=0$, so $\bigcap_p \mathrm{aff}(X_p\setminus\{a_i\})\ne\emptyset$, contradicting the second part of LP433.1.

nodes.name: Take $r-1$ randomly rotated regular simplices
nodes.statement: Choose $r-1$ random rotations of the regular simplex inscribed in the unit sphere of $\mathbb{R}^d$, with vertex sets $V_1,\ldots,V_{r-1}$.

nodes.name: Add origin and form $V$
nodes.statement: Let $v_n$ be the origin and set $V = \{v_n\} \cup \bigcup_{p=1}^{r-1} V_p$; then $v_n \in \bigcap_{p=1}^{r-1} \mathrm{conv}\,V_p$.

nodes.name: Perturb each vertex within $\delta$-ball
nodes.statement: For every $v \in V$, pick $v^* \in B(v,\delta)$ generically; for small $\delta>0$, $v_n^* \in \bigcap_{p=1}^{r-1} \mathrm{conv}\,V_p^*$ with $V_p^* = \{v^*: v\in V_p\}$.

nodes.name: Return $V^*$ in a-general position
nodes.statement: Choose the perturbations so that $V^*$ (and optionally $B \cup V^*$) is in a-general position; return $V^*$.

nodes.name: Initialise: $t \leftarrow 0$ with current partition $\mathcal{P}$
nodes.statement: Start with $t_0=0$ and the existing $r$-divisible partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}$; this is a regular value.

nodes.name: While loop over singular values
nodes.statement: While $t<1$: locate the next singular value $t_1$ using EP433.4; if $t_1\ge 1$, exit; otherwise determine the unique vanishing index $h$ via Claim ClP433.2.

nodes.name: Swap $a_h$ from $X_q$ into some $X_j$ with $|X_j|\le d$
nodes.statement: Choose $j \in J = \{p\ne q : |X_p|\le d\}$ such that $\det \overline{M^j}(t)<0$ on $L(t_1,\eps_2)$; set $\mathcal{P}\leftarrow \mathcal{P}_j$ (move $a_h$ to $X_j$).

nodes.name: Advance to next regular value
nodes.statement: Continue with $t\leftarrow t_1+\eps_3$ where the new partition $\mathcal{P}^*$ satisfies $\beta_i(t)>0$ for all $i$, giving a new regular value.

nodes.name: Return Tverberg partition at $t=1$
nodes.statement: After finitely many singular values, $t$ reaches $1$; return the resulting Tverberg partition of $\{b_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n\}$.
